study.notes: STUDY: SURPASS-3 MRI, the prespecified MRI substudy of the randomised open label parallel group phase 3 SURPASS-3 trial (NCT03882970) at 45 centres in eight countries; adults with type 2 diabetes, HbA1c 7.0 to 10.5 per cent, BMI 25 or more, insulin naive, on metformin with or without an SGLT2 inhibitor, and for the substudy a fatty liver index of 60 or more; randomised 1:1:1:1 to once weekly tirzepatide 5, 10 or 15 mg or once daily titrated insulin degludec; 296 of 502 assessed formed the enrolled MRI population (71, 79, 72 and 74). HOW THIS CAME TO BE EXTRACTED: group 146 had been closed as no_usable_contrast, correctly for the conference abstract it holds, which keeps every number in a table it does not carry. It was reopened on 16 October after src/packet_grouping_check.py showed that the packet bundles two unrelated studies and that the SURPASS-3 record had never been assessed on its own (docs/PACKET_GROUPING_TRIAGE.md). A first pass took the pooled 10 and 15 mg liver fat contrast from the indexed abstract; this extraction REPLACES that single row with the six dose specific contrasts of the article's Table 2, read through the institutional route on ScienceDirect and captured to work/fulltext/companion/surpass3_mri_gastaldelli2022_table2.txt. SURPASS-3 was not otherwise in the corpus and these are the first liver fat and visceral fat contrasts of the GLP-1 and GIP class. SCALE: Table 2 prints, for each marker, the absolute change with its estimated treatment difference AND the relative change from baseline with its own estimated treatment difference. The relative rows are already the comparator corrected percent change the pipeline pools, so every row here is measure PCT on the relative estimated treatment difference and needs no baseline denominator; the absolute differences are in the capture for the audit and are not entered, because entering both would double count the arm. NOT EXTRACTED: neither adiponectin nor leptin appears anywhere in the article's main text or tables, although the substudy's own conference abstract states that all tirzepatide doses increased adiponectin and decreased leptin against insulin degludec; those two belong to the appendix of clinical and laboratory parameters and stay in the supplement queue. Table 2 carries no body weight row, so pct_weight_change is empty on all six rows and they are outside the weight adjusted meta-regression; the abstract gives only a correlation of the liver fat change with the weight change (rho 0.34). Abdominal subcutaneous fat, visceral fat as a percentage of total abdominal fat, the visceral to subcutaneous ratio and the proportions reaching liver fat targets are reported and are not inventory keys. industry_funded TRUE: Eli Lilly and Company. The second study in this packet, a liraglutide muscle fat infiltration trial, remains no_usable_contrast

json.design: prespecified MRI substudy of a randomised open label parallel group phase 3 trial, 52 weeks
other_markers: HbA1c and body weight of the main trial
tables_used: Table 2 of Gastaldelli 2022 (companion capture, institutional route)

rob.justification: d1 low: randomised 1:1:1:1 centrally by an interactive web response system and stratified by country, HbA1c and concomitant oral agent. d2 some_concerns: the trial is open label, a weekly injection against a titrated daily insulin, although the endpoint here is an imaging measure rather than a behavioural or reported one. d3 some_concerns: 296 of the 502 assessed entered the enrolled MRI population, which is the modified intention to treat set with a valid MRI at baseline or after, and the abstract gives no attrition by arm. d4 low: MRI proton density fat fraction, a quantitative imaging measure read centrally. d5 low: this is the substudy's prespecified primary endpoint, reported with its interval.

doubts: the six rows are the relative change estimated treatment differences; the absolute differences of the same table are deliberately not entered, because both would double count the arm
adiponectin and leptin are described as improved against the comparator in the substudy's own conference abstract and appear nowhere in the article, so they stay in the supplement queue
Table 2 has no body weight row, so these rows carry no pct_weight_change and are outside the weight adjusted meta-regression
the trial is open label, although the extracted endpoints are quantitative imaging measures
